title: Punctuation Omitted

illustrates.quote: f. A transcriber's note is not required when converting uppercase to lowercase, omitting font attributes, or omitting punctuation. (See Sample 11-13: Punctuation Omitted on page 11-38.)

print.notes: A note above the table states: "This sample is technical foreign language Portuguese." (BANA Errata March 2024, C8: the book originally mislabeled the language as French; the vocabulary is Portuguese prepositions/articles).
print.surroundingText: "Note: This sample is technical foreign language Portuguese." appears above the table caption.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box, two-row column heading ("article défini" spanning masc./fém. sub-columns); header cells bold.

lines: pr=p  masc sg  masc pl  f=m sg  f=m pl
braille.notes: Line 1 placeholder "text". Per rule 11.7.1.c/e/f, accent marks and periods on abbreviations are omitted without a transcriber's note: "prép." becomes "prep" (no accent, no period), "masc. sg." becomes "masc sg" (no periods), "à"/"às" appear without their accent grave, matching rule 11.7.1.e (punctuation may be omitted) applied silently.

uncertain: Whether the missing accent marks (e.g. in 'a', 'a') in the braille are because literary braille has no distinct accented-letter cells in this technical-Portuguese context, or because they were omitted per some other rule, was not resolved -- recorded as transcribed, not re-derived.
resolution: No content differences beyond header-schema normalization; both runs' 2-row header (prep./article defini spanning 4 sub-columns) matches the PDF image (p. 320).
